subject: sub-09
notes: Manual ICA decisions after reviewing topographies and properties.

0.label: eye_blink_artifact
0.notes: Topography shows strong frontal positivity maximal at Fp1/Fp2 with diffuse posterior negativity — classic eye blink/EOG pattern. Time course shows slow drifts and transient bursts. Extremely high variance outliers (>1000 AU). Reject.

1.label: eye_blink_artifact
1.notes: Topography shows broad frontal negativity (blue) with inferior positivity — consistent with vertical EOG/blink. Time course shows slow undulating drift. One extreme variance outlier (~900 AU). Reject.

2.label: edge_artifact
2.notes: Topography shows a very focal, non-dipolar negativity concentrated at the frontocentral midline with concentric contours and no clear opposing pole — overly focal hotspot. Spectrum shows prominent 60 Hz peak. Sharp transient spike visible in time course. Reject.

3.label: global_noise_component
3.notes: Topography is entirely uniform deep blue with no dipolar structure — global, non-dipolar field. Segment image shows diffuse, sustained horizontal streaks across all segments. Not a neural source. Reject.

4.label: mixed_component
4.notes: Topography shows an overly focal blue hotspot at left centroparietal region on a broad orange background — not a clean dipole. Segment image shows dense, sustained activity across many epochs suggestive of alpha/non-neural contamination. Reject.

5.label: edge_artifact
5.notes: Topography shows a focal right frontotemporal hotspot with no clear opposing pole — non-dipolar edge pattern. Time course shows a large transient spike at onset. Very high variance outliers (>1500 AU) clustered early. Reject.

6.label: mixed_component
6.notes: Topography shows a right frontotemporal focal maximum with left hemisphere negativity — asymmetric and non-dipolar, resembling a muscle or bridging artifact. Spectrum is flat/non-neural. Variance outliers are large and sparse. Reject.

7.label: global_noise_component
7.notes: Topography is predominantly diffuse red across the entire scalp with a small central blue patch — not a dipolar pattern, resembles a global reference artifact. Segment image shows faint persistent horizontal activity. Reject.

8.label: edge_artifact
8.notes: Topography shows bilateral frontal edge maxima (left and right superior frontal) with no clear opposing pole and no posterior structure. Time course shows a large late transient burst. Extreme variance outlier (~8000 AU). Reject.

9.label: edge_artifact
9.notes: Topography shows a very focal blue hotspot at the left temporal/edge region with irregular surrounding contours — non-dipolar edge artifact. Variance shows a large cluster of outliers at the end of the recording. Reject.

10.label: mixed_component
10.notes: Topography shows a broad left frontocentral negativity with weak posterior positivity — not clearly dipolar, asymmetric and spread across the scalp. Spectrum shows elevated and relatively flat power across frequencies. Reject.

11.label: edge_artifact
11.notes: Topography shows a very focal hotspot at the right frontal edge with weak and asymmetric surrounding field — non-dipolar. Time course shows a moderate mid-recording transient. Variance outlier is very large (~1250 AU). Reject.

12.label: edge_artifact
12.notes: Topography shows a very focal blue hotspot at the left temporal edge with no clear opposing pole — classic edge artifact pattern. Variance shows many large outliers (up to ~700 AU) scattered throughout. Reject.

13.label: mixed_component
13.notes: Topography shows a central-left parietal focal maximum surrounded by global blue field — not truly dipolar, the 'opposing pole' is too diffuse and global. Segment image shows sustained low-amplitude widespread activity. Borderline but conservative rejection applies. Reject.

14.label: edge_artifact
14.notes: Topography shows a very focal blue hotspot at the right temporal edge with irregular surrounding contours — non-dipolar edge artifact. Very large variance outliers (>800 AU) throughout. Reject.

15.label: mixed_component

16.label: edge_artifact
